tasks.title: The Filter That Did Not Push Down

description.context: A NordGrid Mid engineer wrote a daily-billing query expecting the filter to push down to the parquet reader. The Spark UI shows the FileScan task reading 12M rows when only 800K should match the filter. The senior engineer asks them to read the plan and identify what stopped the pushdown.
description.task: Why is PushedFilters empty, and what is the fix?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
is_active_meter = udf(lambda mid: mid is not None and len(mid) == 12, 'boolean')

result = (meters
    .filter(is_active_meter(col('meter_id')))
    .filter(col('region') == 'NORTH')
    .agg(sum('daily_kw').alias('total')))

Rows Read Observed: 12M (full table)

Rows Read Expected If Pushdown Worked: 800K (NORTH region only)

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Plan from a 12M-meter daily billing query where a filter that LOOKS push-eligible did not push down

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=false
+- HashAggregate(keys=[], functions=[sum(daily_kw#3)])
   +- Exchange SinglePartition
      +- HashAggregate(keys=[], functions=[partial_sum(daily_kw#3)])
         +- Project [daily_kw#3]
            +- Filter ((region#5 = NORTH) AND pythonUDF0#22)
               +- BatchEvalPython [is_active_meter(meter_id#0)#21], [pythonUDF0#22]
                  +- ColumnarToRow
                     +- FileScan parquet [meter_id#0, daily_kw#3, region#5]
                        PushedFilters: []

fields.label: Why is PushedFilters empty, and what is the fix?
options: PushedFilters is always empty for queries with .agg(); pushdown only works for SELECT queries that return raw rows. Fix: add a .select() before the .agg() to enable pushdown.
The .agg(sum(...)) at the top blocks pushdown because Spark cannot reorder aggregates with filters. Fix: move the aggregation into a subquery so Catalyst can push past it.

The is_active_meter UDF in the FIRST filter forces BatchEvalPython before the second filter. Catalyst stops considering downstream filters once a UDF appears. Fix: replace the UDF with built-in expressions.
The two .filter() calls confuse Catalyst — only the LAST filter ever gets considered for pushdown. Fix: combine both into a single .filter((region == 'NORTH') & is_active_meter(meter_id)) call.
fields.correctAnswer: The is_active_meter UDF in the FIRST filter forces BatchEvalPython before the second filter. Catalyst stops considering downstream filters once a UDF appears. Fix: replace the UDF with built-in expressions.
fields.rationale: Once a Python UDF appears in the chain, Catalyst inserts BatchEvalPython and stops pushing predicates past it.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Invents a 'no pushdown for aggregates' rule.Aggregations don't block pushdown; the UDF does.
Option B: Blames the aggregate.

tasks.title: Two Predicates, One Pushed Down, One Not

description.context: A NordGrid Mid engineer wrote a query with two filter conditions joined by OR. They expected both to push down. The plan shows only ONE in PushedFilters; the other appears as a separate Filter operator. The senior engineer asks: which conditions push down with OR-disjunctions, and which don't?
description.task: Why does Plan A push down but Plan B not, and what is the structural rule?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code A: meters.filter((col('region') == 'NORTH') | (col('region') == 'SOUTH')).explain()

Code B: meters.filter((col('region') == 'NORTH') | (col('daily_kw') > 1000)).explain()

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Two side-by-side plans from queries with OR-disjunctions; one combination pushes, the other doesn't

fields.label: Why does Plan A push down but Plan B not, and what is the structural rule?
options: Plan A pushed because string equality is push-eligible at the file reader level; Plan B's daily_kw comparison is not push-eligible because numeric comparisons require a different mode. Fix: cast daily_kw to string.

Plan A pushed because Catalyst rewrote two equalities on the same column into a single In(region, [NORTH, SOUTH]). Plan B's OR spans two columns; the parquet reader cannot evaluate cross-column predicates.
Plan B did not push because Spark requires AT LEAST 3 conditions to attempt pushdown on disjunctions. Fix: add a third condition (e.g., isNotNull on either column) to trigger pushdown.
Both plans pushed down identically; the missing PushedFilters in Plan B is a display bug in .explain(). The actual file reader behavior is the same — both filters apply at scan time.
fields.correctAnswer: Plan A pushed because Catalyst rewrote two equalities on the same column into a single In(region, [NORTH, SOUTH]). Plan B's OR spans two columns; the parquet reader cannot evaluate cross-column predicates.
fields.rationale: The structural rule is: pushdown works for predicates evaluable from a single column (or simple combinations on one column).
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Invents a string-vs-numeric pushdown distinction.Both types push when single-column.
Option C: Invents a 3-condition rule.

description.context: A NordGrid Mid engineer joined meters (12M rows) with substations (200 rows, ~50KB on disk). They expected Spark to broadcast the tiny substations table automatically. Instead the plan shows SortMergeJoin and the pipeline takes 4× longer than expected. spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold is set to 100MB — well above the 50KB substations file. Why did Catalyst pick sort-merge?
description.task: Why did Catalyst choose SortMergeJoin, and what is the fix?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Left Size: 12M rows (meters)

Right Size On Disk: 50KB (substations parquet file)

Right Size In Memory Estimated: 200MB (Catalyst's stale estimate)

Broadcast Threshold: 100MB (autoBroadcastJoinThreshold)

Last Analyze Table: 18 months ago

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Plan choosing SortMergeJoin over BroadcastHashJoin despite the small side fitting under the broadcast threshold

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=false
+- SortMergeJoin [substation_id#7], [substation_id#19], Inner
   :- Sort [substation_id#7 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
   :  +- Exchange hashpartitioning(substation_id#7, 200)
   :     +- FileScan parquet meters
   +- Sort [substation_id#19 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
      +- Exchange hashpartitioning(substation_id#19, 200)
         +- FileScan parquet substations

# Catalyst's metadata for substations table:
#   sizeInBytes = 209715200 (200MB)
#   rowCount = unknown
#   ANALYZE TABLE last run: 18 months ago, before partitioning scheme changed

fields.label: Why did Catalyst choose SortMergeJoin, and what is the fix?
options: SortMergeJoin is always preferred for inner joins because it is more reliable than broadcast under load. Broadcast hints only matter for outer joins. Fix: nothing — the plan is correct as-is.
SortMergeJoin is always preferred for inner joins because it is more reliable than broadcast under load. Broadcast hints only matter for outer joins. Fix: nothing — the plan is correct.
Catalyst chose SortMergeJoin because spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold is treated as a soft limit; only explicit broadcast() hints actually broadcast. Fix: add broadcast(substations) to force it.
Catalyst metadata says substations is 200MB (above the 100MB threshold). The estimate is stale — it was 200MB 18 months ago but is now 50KB. Fix: ANALYZE TABLE substations COMPUTE STATISTICS.
fields.correctAnswer: Catalyst metadata says substations is 200MB (above the 100MB threshold). The estimate is stale — it was 200MB 18 months ago but is now 50KB. Fix: ANALYZE TABLE substations COMPUTE STATISTICS.
fields.rationale: Catalyst uses table statistics (sizeInBytes, rowCount) from the metadata catalog to decide between broadcast and sort-merge.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: isFinalPlan=false just means the plan was printed pre-execution; AQE may still be enabled.

description.context: A NordGrid Mid engineer added a broadcast hint to speed up a join. The pipeline started failing with driver OOMs after 30 seconds. The plan shows BroadcastExchange building from 12M rows. The engineer is confused — they thought broadcasting helped. The senior engineer asks them to identify which side they hinted to broadcast and why it was wrong.
description.task: What is the bug, and what is the fix?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: result = (broadcast(meters)
    .join(substations, on='substation_id', how='inner')
    .groupBy('region')
    .agg(sum('daily_kw').alias('total')))

Meters Size: 12M rows, ~2.4 GB on disk

Substations Size: 200 rows, ~50KB on disk

Driver Heap: 1g default

Observed Failure: driver OOM during BroadcastExchange build phase

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Plan with broadcast() hint applied to the wrong side (the 12M-row meters), causing driver heap inflation

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=false
+- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22], functions=[sum(daily_kw#3)])
   +- Exchange hashpartitioning(region#22, 200)
      +- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22], functions=[partial_sum(daily_kw#3)])
         +- Project [daily_kw#3, region#22]
            +- BroadcastHashJoin [substation_id#7], [substation_id#19], Inner, BuildLeft
               :- BroadcastExchange HashedRelationBroadcastMode
               :  +- FileScan parquet meters
               +- FileScan parquet substations

# Driver log excerpt:
# WARN BroadcastExchangeExec: Could not execute broadcast in 300s
# org.apache.spark.SparkException: Cannot broadcast the table over the threshold of 8GB

fields.label: What is the bug, and what is the fix?
options: Both sides are being broadcast accidentally; remove the hint entirely and let Catalyst auto-decide based on the available statistics. The BroadcastExchange shouldn't appear at all in this plan if the hint were removed.
Both sides are being broadcast accidentally; remove the hint entirely and let Catalyst auto-decide based on statistics. The BroadcastExchange shouldn't appear at all in this plan.
broadcast() is incompatible with .agg() following the join — Spark cannot fuse the broadcast with the partial aggregate. Fix: split the query into two stages with a .cache() in between.

broadcast(meters) hints the LEFT side (12M rows). BuildLeft confirms Catalyst is materializing 12M rows on the driver as a hash table. Fix: broadcast(substations) — the small side is what should broadcast.
fields.correctAnswer: broadcast(meters) hints the LEFT side (12M rows). BuildLeft confirms Catalyst is materializing 12M rows on the driver as a hash table. Fix: broadcast(substations) — the small side is what should broadcast.
fields.rationale: broadcast(meters) tells Catalyst to use meters as the broadcast (build) side.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Raises the threshold instead of fixing the bug; broadcasting 12M rows is wrong regardless of threshold.

description.context: AQE adapts the plan at runtime based on actual data sizes. After execution, .explain() shows AQEShuffleRead operators with annotations. The most common is 'coalesced' — AQE noticed that some shuffle partitions ended up much smaller than expected, and merged adjacent ones to reduce overhead. The number after 'coalesced' tells you the new partition count; the original count was spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (default 200).
description.task: What did AQE do at runtime, and why?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: (meters.groupBy('region').agg(sum('daily_kw')).collect()) ; df.explain()

Shuffle Partitions: 200

Data Volume After Partial Agg: ~50KB total (4 regions × tiny partial sums)

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Plan with AQEShuffleRead coalesced annotation visible after execution; identify what AQE did and why

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=true
+- HashAggregate(keys=[region#5], functions=[sum(daily_kw#3)])
   +- AQEShuffleRead coalesced
      +- ShuffleQueryStage 0
         +- Exchange hashpartitioning(region#5, 200), [plan_id=14]
            +- HashAggregate(keys=[region#5], functions=[partial_sum(daily_kw#3)])
               +- FileScan parquet meters

# Stage metrics from Spark UI:
#   Original shuffle partitions: 200
#   Coalesced to: 12
#   Bytes per coalesced partition target: 64MB (default)
#   Average actual bytes per coalesced partition: 4.2KB

fields.label: What did AQE do at runtime, and why?
options: AQE ran into a shuffle service failure on 188 of the 200 partitions and was forced to fall back to 12. The coalesced annotation is a recovery indicator, not an optimization.

AQE detected post-shuffle data was tiny (50KB total) and merged 200 partitions into 12 to reduce task scheduling overhead. Reading 200 nearly-empty partitions is wasteful; 12 is closer to the natural cardinality.
AQE sampled the data and decided 12 was the optimal partition count for the next stage's parallelism; this is unrelated to data volume. The 4.2KB per partition is incidental.
AQE coalesced because the engineer set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to 12 in their config; the 200 in the Exchange line is what Catalyst printed at planning time but the runtime value is 12.
fields.correctAnswer: AQE detected post-shuffle data was tiny (50KB total) and merged 200 partitions into 12 to reduce task scheduling overhead. Reading 200 nearly-empty partitions is wasteful; 12 is closer to the natural cardinality.
fields.rationale: AQE's coalescePartitions feature watches the actual size of shuffle output stages.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes), AQE merges adjacent ones.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Treats coalesced as failure recovery; it is an optimization, not a fallback.

tasks.title: AQE Local — The Skew Split Worked

description.context: AQE has a second optimization that fires when one shuffle partition is much larger than its peers (the skew case). AQE detects the skew at runtime and splits that one large partition into multiple sub-partitions — labelled 'local' in the AQEShuffleRead annotation. The notation '1→8' means one skewed partition was split into 8 sub-partitions, each handling roughly an eighth of the original work in parallel. This is AQE's skew handling, distinct from coalescing.
description.task: Which side was skewed, and what does '1 → 8' tell you?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: meters.join(events_log, on='meter_id', how='inner').agg(...)

Skew Factor Observed: 12× (one meter_id had 12× more rows than the average)

Shuffle Partitions: 200

Skew Threshold: spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionFactor=5

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Plan with AQEShuffleRead local annotation showing a skew partition split; identify which side was skewed and the resulting parallelism

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=true
+- SortMergeJoin [meter_id#0], [meter_id#100], Inner
   :- Sort [meter_id#0 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
   :  +- AQEShuffleRead local (skew partition split: 1 → 8)
   :     +- ShuffleQueryStage 0
   :        +- Exchange hashpartitioning(meter_id#0, 200), [plan_id=12]
   :           +- FileScan parquet meters
   +- Sort [meter_id#100 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
      +- AQEShuffleRead
         +- ShuffleQueryStage 1
            +- Exchange hashpartitioning(meter_id#100, 200), [plan_id=14]
               +- FileScan parquet events_log

fields.label: Which side was skewed, and what does '1 → 8' tell you?
options: Both sides were skewed equally; AQE applied the same split to each. The annotation only appears on one side as a display optimization but both sides have 8 sub-partitions now.
Neither side was skewed; the local annotation appears on every shuffle and means localized read. The 1 → 8 is a partition placement detail unrelated to skew handling at runtime.

The meters side (top branch) was skewed. AQE detected a partition with 12× the average size, exceeding the 5× threshold, and split that partition into 8 sub-partitions. The events_log side has no annotation.
The events_log side (bottom branch) was skewed; the local annotation on the meters side is what enables the OTHER side's skew handling. Skew handling always annotates the opposite side.
fields.correctAnswer: The meters side (top branch) was skewed. AQE detected a partition with 12× the average size, exceeding the 5× threshold, and split that partition into 8 sub-partitions. The events_log side has no annotation.
fields.rationale: Read where the local annotation appears: only on the meters branch.That tells you AQE detected skew on the meters side specifically.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Treats skew as symmetric.AQE's split is per-side; the annotation is where the action happened.
Option B: Treats local as cosmetic.

tasks.title: The Broadcast() Hint That Catalyst Ignored

description.context: A NordGrid Mid engineer added broadcast(customer_dim) expecting Catalyst to broadcast the customer_dim table. The plan still shows SortMergeJoin and the engineer is confused — why didn't the hint take effect? The senior engineer points out that broadcast() hints are SUGGESTIONS, not commands. Catalyst silently ignores hints when the wrapped side exceeds spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold.
description.task: Why did Catalyst ignore the broadcast() hint, and what is the resolution?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: result = (meters
    .join(broadcast(customer_dim), on='customer_id', how='inner')
    .agg(...))

Customer Dim Size: 200MB on disk (~340MB hash relation in memory)

Broadcast Threshold: 100MB

Expected Plan: BroadcastHashJoin

Actual Plan: SortMergeJoin

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Plan where broadcast() hint was applied to a 200MB table with autoBroadcastJoinThreshold=100MB; Catalyst ignored the hint

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=false
+- SortMergeJoin [customer_id#0], [customer_id#50], Inner
   :- Sort [customer_id#0 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
   :  +- Exchange hashpartitioning(customer_id#0, 200)
   :     +- FileScan parquet meters
   +- Sort [customer_id#50 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
      +- Exchange hashpartitioning(customer_id#50, 200)
         +- FileScan parquet customer_dim

fields.label: Why did Catalyst ignore the broadcast() hint, and what is the resolution?
options: customer_dim is 200MB. That exceeds the 100MB autoBroadcastJoinThreshold. Catalyst silently ignores broadcast() hints when the wrapped side is over the threshold. Fix: raise threshold or shrink the table.
broadcast() hints only work in SQL; the DataFrame API form is parsed but never applied. Resolution: rewrite as spark.sql('SELECT /*+ BROADCAST(customer_dim) */ ...') to make the hint take effect.
AdaptiveSparkPlan with isFinalPlan=false means AQE has not adapted yet; broadcast hints only apply post-AQE. Resolution: call .collect() first so AQE runs and the hint takes effect.

The hint conflicts with the implicit broadcast threshold; Catalyst applies a XOR rule where exactly ONE source of broadcast pressure must exist. Resolution: remove the hint and rely on the threshold alone.
fields.correctAnswer: customer_dim is 200MB. That exceeds the 100MB autoBroadcastJoinThreshold. Catalyst silently ignores broadcast() hints when the wrapped side is over the threshold. Fix: raise threshold or shrink the table.
fields.distractorRationale: Option B: Treats DataFrame broadcast() as broken; both forms work identically when applicable.

description.context: A NordGrid Mid engineer added .repartition(400) to fight skew on a join; they wanted more parallelism. The pipeline still ran slow. The plan reveals that downstream code in another file added .coalesce(20) before the write. Coalesce after repartition can defeat the repartition entirely. The engineer didn't write the .coalesce() — it was added by a colleague six months ago. The plan tells the story.
description.task: What happened to the .repartition(400), and what is the architectural lesson?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: skewed = meters.join(events_log, on='meter_id', how='inner')
repartitioned = skewed.repartition(400, col('meter_id'))
result = repartitioned.groupBy('region').agg(sum('value').alias('total'))
result.coalesce(20).write.parquet('output/')

Expected Join Parallelism: 400

Actual Join Parallelism Observed: 20

Skew Persisted: yes — same long-tail tasks as before repartition

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: Plan where .repartition(400) was added to fight skew but a downstream .coalesce(20) consolidated back, defeating the repartition

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=false
+- WriteFiles parquet output/
   +- Coalesce 20
      +- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22], functions=[sum(value#3)])
         +- Exchange hashpartitioning(region#22, 200)
            +- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22], functions=[partial_sum(value#3)])
               +- Project [region#22, value#3]
                  +- SortMergeJoin [meter_id#0], [meter_id#100], Inner
                     :- Sort [meter_id#0 ASC], false
                     :  +- Exchange hashpartitioning(meter_id#0, 200)
                     :     +- FileScan parquet meters
                     +- Sort [meter_id#100 ASC], false
                        +- Exchange hashpartitioning(meter_id#100, 200)
                           +- FileScan parquet events_log

fields.label: What happened to the .repartition(400), and what is the architectural lesson?
options: Catalyst removed .repartition(400) entirely as a redundant operation because the join already shuffles. The engineer's repartition was wasted code; the plan never included it. Lesson: repartitions before joins are no-ops.

The .repartition(400) is in the plan but invisible because Catalyst optimized it into the Exchange nodes; partition counts of 200 in the plan reflect AQE's coalesce, not the original 400. Lesson: AQE always overrides explicit repartitions.

Catalyst eliminated the .repartition(400) because the downstream .coalesce(20) made it pointless — repartitioning to 400 just to coalesce to 20 is wasted shuffle. The Exchange shows the 200 default, NOT 400. Lesson: read the whole pipeline before tuning a stage.

The plan shows .repartition(400) successfully applied via the SortMergeJoin's Exchange operators (which use 400 partitions). The visible 200 is a display abbreviation; the actual runtime parallelism is 400. Lesson: trust the code over the plan.
fields.correctAnswer: Catalyst eliminated the .repartition(400) because the downstream .coalesce(20) made it pointless — repartitioning to 400 just to coalesce to 20 is wasted shuffle. The Exchange shows the 200 default, NOT 400. Lesson: read the whole pipeline before tuning a stage.
fields.rationale: coalesce(20) downstream means the 400 will never be observed — it gets re-merged before output.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Treats repartition before joins as universally redundant; repartition serves multiple purposes.

description.context: A NordGrid Mid engineer claims they tuned a daily-billing pipeline with broadcast hint, AQE, and explicit predicate pushdown. They show the senior the pipeline code AND the resulting plan and ask for review. The senior asks the engineer to verify EACH tuning intervention by reading the plan — not by trusting the code. Five sub-questions audit the five tuning claims.

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: 50-line tuned pipeline at NordGrid Mid scale; verify each tuning claim against the plan output

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
# Pipeline code
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.adaptive.enabled', 'true')
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled', 'true')
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold', '50m')

result = (meters
    .filter(col('daily_kw') > 100)
    .filter(col('region').isin(['NORTH', 'SOUTH']))
    .join(broadcast(substations), on='substation_id', how='inner')
    .groupBy('region', 'capacity_mw')
    .agg(sum('daily_kw').alias('total_kw'), count('*').alias('n_meters'))
    .repartition(20))
result.collect()
result.explain()

# Substations stats: 200 rows, 50KB on disk
# Plan output (post-execution):

== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=true
+- AQEShuffleRead coalesced
   +- ShuffleQueryStage 2
      +- Exchange RoundRobinPartitioning(20), [plan_id=88]
         +- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22, capacity_mw#28], functions=[sum(daily_kw#3), count(1)])
            +- AQEShuffleRead coalesced
               +- ShuffleQueryStage 1
                  +- Exchange hashpartitioning(region#22, capacity_mw#28, 200), [plan_id=44]
                     +- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22, capacity_mw#28], functions=[partial_sum(daily_kw#3), partial_count(1)])
                        +- Project [daily_kw#3, region#22, capacity_mw#28]
                           +- BroadcastHashJoin [substation_id#7], [substation_id#19], Inner, BuildRight
                              :- Filter ((isnotnull(daily_kw#3) AND (daily_kw#3 > 100.0)) AND region#5 IN (NORTH, SOUTH))
                              :  +- ColumnarToRow
                              :     +- FileScan parquet [meter_id#0, daily_kw#3, region#5, substation_id#7]
                              :        PushedFilters: [IsNotNull(daily_kw), GreaterThan(daily_kw,100.0), In(region, [NORTH, SOUTH]), IsNotNull(substation_id)]
                              +- BroadcastExchange HashedRelationBroadcastMode
                                 +- FileScan parquet substations

description.context: Final exercise of the Mid track. A NordGrid pipeline runs correctly but is suboptimal. The senior asks the engineer to read the plan and identify FIVE missed plan-level tuning opportunities. Each one is a different category: missed pushdown, missed broadcast eligibility, AQE skew handling not engaged, partition over-count, predicate after join instead of before. The plan tells the story; the code looks fine on its own.

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: 55-line NordGrid Mid pipeline with five embedded missed plan-level tuning opportunities

evidence.label: Snippet
evidence.content:
# Pipeline code
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.adaptive.enabled', 'true')
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled', 'true')
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.shuffle.partitions', '800')
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold', '10m')  # default

is_active = udf(lambda s: s == 'ACTIVE', 'boolean')

result = (meters
    .join(customer_dim, on='customer_id', how='left_outer')   # customer_dim 8MB
    .filter(is_active(col('status')))
    .filter(col('region') == 'NORTH')
    .groupBy('region', 'customer_type')
    .agg(sum('daily_kw').alias('total_kw')))

result.collect()
result.explain()

== Physical Plan ==
AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=true
+- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22, customer_type#33], functions=[sum(daily_kw#3)])
   +- AQEShuffleRead coalesced
      +- ShuffleQueryStage 1
         +- Exchange hashpartitioning(region#22, customer_type#33, 800), [plan_id=66]
            +- HashAggregate(keys=[region#22, customer_type#33], functions=[partial_sum(daily_kw#3)])
               +- Project [region#22, customer_type#33, daily_kw#3]
                  +- Filter (region#22 = NORTH)
                     +- Filter pythonUDF0#88: boolean
                        +- BatchEvalPython [is_active(status#11)#87], [pythonUDF0#88]
                           +- SortMergeJoin [customer_id#0], [customer_id#50], LeftOuter
                              :- Sort [customer_id#0 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
                              :  +- Exchange hashpartitioning(customer_id#0, 800)
                              :     +- FileScan parquet meters
                              +- Sort [customer_id#50 ASC NULLS FIRST], false
                                 +- Exchange hashpartitioning(customer_id#50, 800)
                                    +- FileScan parquet customer_dim
                                       PushedFilters: []
